reference_sql:
SELECT promo_code, 'start' AS event, start_date AS event_date
FROM promotions
WHERE start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-06-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'
UNION ALL
SELECT promo_code, 'end', end_date
FROM promotions
WHERE start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-06-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'
alternatives: WITH events AS (SELECT 'start' AS event UNION ALL SELECT 'end') SELECT p.promo_code, e.event, CASE WHEN e.event = 'start' THEN p.start_date ELSE p.end_date END AS event_date FROM promotions p CROSS JOIN events e WHERE p.start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-06-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'

SELECT promo_code, 'end' AS event, end_date AS event_date FROM promotions WHERE start_date >= DATE '2025-06-01' AND start_date < DATE '2025-07-01' UNION ALL SELECT promo_code, 'start', start_date FROM promotions WHERE start_date >= DATE '2025-06-01' AND start_date < DATE '2025-07-01'

other_way.sql: WITH events AS (SELECT 'start' AS event UNION ALL SELECT 'end') SELECT p.promo_code, e.event, CASE WHEN e.event = 'start' THEN p.start_date ELSE p.end_date END AS event_date FROM promotions p CROSS JOIN events e WHERE p.start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-06-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'
other_way.tradeoff: A CROSS JOIN with a two-row list and a CASE gives the same rows, but two plain branches are easier to read.
